ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantee for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We propose a new analysis of KernelSHAP's sample complexity using martingale concentration inequalities. This would involve assuming a bounded variance of the noise in the regression problem, and deriving a non-asymptotic bound on the difference between KernelSHAP's estimate and the true Shapley values, as a function of the number of sampled subsets.
CONTROLS: We compare our bounds to those derived from existing unbiased estimators such as Unbiased KernelSHAP.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: If our analysis is successful, we expect to obtain a clear picture of the tradeoff between the number of samples and the accuracy of the KernelSHAP estimate, and possibly outperform existing estimators in certain regimes. The method may fail for very high-dimensional data or data with highly varying subset values.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LeverageSHAP for High-Dimensional Input: A Preprocessing-Based Approach
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the success of LeverageSHAP in reducing variance, we propose a preprocessing-based approach to apply LeverageSHAP to high-dimensional inputs. This would involve first reducing the dimensionality of the input data using principal component analysis or random projections, and then applying LeverageSHAP to the reduced data.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to direct applications of LeverageSHAP or KernelSHAP to high-dimensional inputs.
COST: 6500
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to demonstrate the feasibility of LeverageSHAP for high-dimensional inputs, and potentially reduce the computational cost of this efficient estimator. This method may fail if the dimensionality reduction loses too much information about the input data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Analyzing the Tradeoffs between KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework to compare the tradeoffs between KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP in terms of bias, variance, and computational cost. This framework would involve deriving theoretical bounds for both estimators, and using the bounds to identify scenarios in which one estimator outperforms the other.
CONTROLS: We examine the parameters that influence the tradeoffs, such as the dimensionality of the input data and the number of samples.
COST: 8500
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to provide a deeper understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, and identify best practices for choosing between these estimators in different situations. This framework may fail to capture all relevant aspects of the estimators' behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A New Sampling Distribution for KernelSHAP: Improving Accuracy through Variance Reduction
PROPOSAL: Building on the idea of reweighting subsets in the KernelSHAP formulation, we propose a new sampling distribution that balances the need to accurately estimate kernel weights with the desire to reduce variance. This distribution would involve stratified sampling with adaptive stratification based on subset difficulty.
CONTROLS: We compare our distribution to the standard sampling distribution used in KernelSHAP, and to other adaptive sampling schemes in the literature.
COST: 9500
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to demonstrate improvements in the accuracy of the KernelSHAP estimate, particularly in high-dimensional settings. Our method may fail to generalize to all types of data or models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Model-Assisted Approach to Computing Shapley Values in High Dimensions
PROPOSAL: To address the computational challenges of high-dimensional Shapley value computation, we propose a two-stage approach that leverages the statistical properties of the model to reduce the dimensionality of the input space. In the first stage, we train a flexible model to provide an initial approximation of the Shapley values. In the second stage, we use a local model to refine this approximation.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to direct computation of Shapley values in high dimensions, and to other model-assisted approaches in the literature.
COST: 13000
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to provide a scalable approach to computing Shapley values in high dimensions, while maintaining a reasonable level of accuracy. Our method may fail if the initial approximation is poor, or if the local refinement stage overfits to the data.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantee for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We revise our initial proposal to incorporate additionalitivity of Shapley values by applying a cutting-plane method to the kernel weights, which would reduce the theoretical sample complexity bound and make it more practically applicable.
CONTROLS: We compare our bounds to those obtained from additional estimators.
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: If our revising approach is successful, we expect to derive a practical and less conservative bound on the sample complexity, allowing researchers to apply KernelSHAP with fewer samples and outperform existing estimators. This approach might fail if the cutting-plane method does not converge quickly enough.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Shapley Values to Adversarial Perturbations
PROPOSAL: Motivated by the increasing concern for robustness in machine learning, we propose an experimental investigation into the stability of Shapley values under adversarial perturbations of the input data. We will examine how different estimators (including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and our proposed model-assisted approach) respond to such perturbations.
CONTROLS: We compare the robustness of different estimators to common adversarial attacks such as FGSM and PGD.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to gain insights into the limitations of current Shapley value estimators and identify potential opportunities for improvement. Our findings may highlight vulnerabilities in existing methods and suggest new research directions. However, our results could also indicate inherent instability in Shapley values, limiting their applicability in certain contexts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: KernelSHAP for Non-Linear Models: An Approximation Using Bootstrap Sampling
PROPOSAL: When applying KernelSHAP to non-linear models, the high computational cost of evaluating the model on each subset can be prohibitive. We propose a novel approximation method leveraging bootstrap sampling to efficiently estimate the output of the model on each subset, at a fraction of the computational cost.
CONTROLS: We compare our approximation to the standard KernelSHAP method and examine its impact on estimation accuracy.
COST: 22000
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to make KernelSHAP applicable to non-linear models, with a focus on reducing computation time while maintaining accuracy. However, the accuracy of the method may depend on the specifics of the model and dataset, and may degrade for certain types of models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Public Dataset for Evaluating and Comparing Shapley Value Estimators
PROPOSAL: We propose the creation of a public dataset that captures the complexities of real-world data and allows for a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of different Shapley value estimators. Our dataset would include a wide range of models, inputs, and ground-truth Shapley values.
CONTROLS: We seront chose the contents and format of the dataset by surveying the existing body of work on Shapley values and by querying practitioners in the field.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to facilitate approval comparison and evaluation of the proposed estimators on real-world data. However, creating such a comprehensive dataset is a challenging task that requires consulting a broad range of stakeholders and experts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Scalable and Interpretable Algorithm for Global Sensitivity Analysis using Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Building on our research, we propose a new algorithm that leverages the power of Shapley values to perform global sensitivity analysis on complex systems. Our algorithm would be scalable and interpretable, allowing users to easily identify the most critical factors driving system behavior.
CONTROLS: We compare our algorithm to existing methods for global sensitivity analysis and examine its performance on a range of applications.
COST: 38000
PREDICTION: If successful, we expect to provide a novel tool for global sensitivity analysis that is both scalable and interpretable, facilitating the analysis of complex systems in various fields. However, the development of this algorithm is a challenging task that requires combining insights from multiple areas of research.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Temporally-Weighted Transformers for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: We will adapt multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with a temporally-weighted attention mechanism to weight the importance of past events in the sequence, and compare two variants with (i) exponentially decaying weights and (ii) attention weights learned from task data.
CONTROLS: We will compare these variants against a standard transformer decoder and a modified variant that uses a uniform temporal weighting scheme.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: The temporally-weighted variants should achieve higher ROUGE scores and a better descriptive coherence metric than the baseline transformer decoder, and the variant with learned weights should outperform the one with exponential decay. This approach may struggle to capture regime changes, such as sudden shifts in land use.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating Hybrid MLLM-Diffusion Pipelines for Temporal Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will design a hybrid model combining the semantic depth of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with the strong image synthesis capabilities of diffusion-based models. Our MLLM component will generate a detailed spatial map of changes, which will be used as input to a diffusion model to generate the corresponding image.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hybrid model against a naive combination of separate MLLM and diffusion components, and against state-of-the-art diffusion-based models.
COST: 35,000
PREDICTION: Our hybrid model should produce temporally consistent forecasts that capture the semantic drivers of change, with improvements in FID and SSIM scores compared to baseline models. However, this approach might require significant computational resources due to the two-stage generation process.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Development of a Multimodal Long-Range Temporal Reasoning Dataset for Satellite Imagery
PROPOSAL: We will create a new dataset consisting of sequences of satellite images annotated with detailed temporal narratives, including information about land use changes, environmental events, and human activities. The dataset will be designed to support both tasks of temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting.
CONTROLS: We will compare performance on our dataset to existing baselines for temporal change description and future forecasting tasks, and evaluate the robustness of our models to out-of-distribution events.
COST: 18,000
PREDICTION: Our dataset should enable more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of models for temporal change description and future forecasting, with particular attention to the ability to reason about long-range temporal dynamics and underlying causal narratives. However, dataset creation and annotation might be time-consuming, and the dataset may not capture all possible real-world scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Assessing the Impact of Temporal Regularization on Model Performance
PROPOSAL: We will explore the effect of incorporating temporal regularization terms into our models' loss functions to encourage long-range temporal consistency. Two variants will be tested: (i) a penalty on changes in the model's output over time and (ii) a term rewarding models that accurately anticipate future changes.
CONTROLS: We will compare these variants against a baseline model without temporal regularization and against a variant using a fill-in gap method that leverages the dataset but isn’t motivated by a clear theoretical justification, to determine whether this technique offers any generalizable advantages over datasets which provide the history of all time steps a given modle will be at those time steps.
COST: 27,000
PREDICTION: Temporal regularization should improve the models' ability to reason about long-range temporal dynamics, captured by metrics of the consistency with forecasts, and help prevent overfitting to short-time scales. However, the choice of regularization terms and their hyperparameters could be crucial and may require careful tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Development of a Multimodal Long-Range Temporal Reasoning Dataset for Satellite Imagery (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We will enhance our dataset with an additional split supporting transfer learning for temporal change description and future forecasting tasks, consisting of sequences with differing start points and end points in time, ensuring islands of continuity for in-sample sequences. Our dataset will be designed to support both tasks of temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting.
CONTROLS: We will compare performance on our dataset to existing baselines for temporal change description and future forecasting tasks, and evaluate the robustness of our models to out-of-distribution events.
COST: 30,000
PREDICTION: Our revised dataset with the supporting transfer learning setup will enable more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of models for temporal change description and future forecasting, with considerations to island of continuity existing more robust and fullivan models.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Diagnostic Analysis of Temporal Change Description Errors
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a qualitative analysis to identify specific sources of error for our models' temporal change description, focusing on cases where models disagree with human annotators. Our analysis will examine the temporal context, geospatial information, and narrative resolution of each failed case.
CONTROLS: We will also compare the frequency and patterns of errors between different models and variants.
COST: 24,000
PREDICTION: This analysis will provide valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of our models and highlight areas for improvement, enabling targeted modifications and refinements. However, a detailed analysis might require significant time and effort, and could become a stopping point of progress if certain changes turn incorrect.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Lower Bounds for Long-Range Temporal Dynamics Prediction
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the regime in which the expected loss of a model for predicting long-range temporal dynamics is bounded from below by a function of the sequence's intrinsic complexity. We will derive a formal expression for this lower bound and analyze the conditions under which the bound is achieved.
CONTROLS: We will compare the derived lower bound to the performance of our trained models on the datasets.
COST: 43,000
PREDICTION: This theoretical result should provide insights into the fundamental limits of performance for models on long-range temporal dynamics prediction tasks and shed light on the properties of the data that are crucial for such prediction. However, translating these results into practical algorithms that can achieve the derived lower bounds may be challenging and could be a subject of further work.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Evaluation Metrics for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a novel set of metrics that specifically evaluate the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts, measuring how well the generated changes agree with the trends observed in the historical data. Our metrics will be designed to complement the existing image-quality metrics used in the field.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our models on these new metrics against standard image-quality metrics, as well as against human evaluations of temporal consistency.
COST: 36,000
PREDICTION: Our temporally consistent evaluation metrics should provide a more comprehensive assessment of a model's ability to capture the underlying temporal dynamics of a scene, allowing us to better evaluate and compare models on this critical aspect of satellite image forecasting. However, the evaluation process might become biased in favor of models that simply mimic observed trends rather than genuinely capturing the underlying causes of change.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Sequential Satellite Imagery on Model Training Dynamics
PROPOSAL: We will study the effect of sequential satellite imagery on model training, specifically how the models adapt to learn from sequences of images that capture gradual changes in the scene. We will compare the performance of models trained on individual images versus sequences of images.
CONTROLS: We will also investigate the impact of sequence length and temporal gap between images on model performance.
COST: 67,000
PREDICTION: This analysis will provide insights into how models learn from sequential satellite imagery and how to optimize training protocols for better performance. However, the study might reveal challenges in model training and adaptation to changing scenes, such as the impact of sequence length and temporal gaps.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: A Multimodal Fusion Framework for Transfer Learning in Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a multimodal fusion framework that combines the strengths of different modalities for transfer learning in satellite image time series forecasting. Our framework will leverage both visual and textual information from satellite images and corresponding narratives, enabling models to learn transferable representations across domains and tasks.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our framework on a range of satellite image datasets with diverse designated application tasks.
COST: 213,000
PREDICTION: Our multimodal fusion framework should improve transfer learning performance in satellite image time series forecasting, enabling models to adapt better to new domains and tasks. However, the complexity of our framework might make it challenging to train and tune, and may require large datasets for effective learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Examining the Impact of Model Component Adaptation in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experimental study by adapting a pre-trained deep forecasting model for time series prediction, updating either the final prediction layer or a small adapter module, and comparing its performance to the base model which is frozen and not updated.
CONTROLS: We will use the base model as a reference point, and also compare the two adaptation strategies by updating only the final prediction layer or a small adapter module.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect that updating the model component will improve forecasting accuracy for adapting to concept drift in real-world time series data, but also introduce some risk of overfitting; the adapter module might have better stability and generalizability than the final prediction layer in some cases, but might not fully capture the changes in data distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Distribution Shift Normalization in Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an online time series forecasting experiment where we forecast multiple steps ahead, apply several normalization techniques to the input data, such as min-max scaling, standardization, and normalization with sample statistics, and evaluate the performance of a pre-trained deep forecasting model on real-world datasets with different types of distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: We will use historical data from the past 500 days as the training data, and the next 100 days as the testing data. We will compare the baseline performance of a frozen model to different normalization techniques applied online.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: We expect that normalization techniques will help in improving the forecasting performance by reducing the effect of covariate shift, but it might not fully handle concept drift; we also expect to see varying results across different datasets and normalization techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Development of a New Online Gradient Descent Method with Ensemble-based Adaptive Learning Rate Scheduling
PROPOSAL: We will develop an online gradient descent method that uses an ensemble of models to adaptively adjust the learning rate based on the recent loss history and forecast performance, and apply it to online time series forecasting tasks on real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method against a variety of other online gradient descent methods, including those with static learning rate schedules and automatic learning rate scheduling techniques. We will also investigate the effect of different ensemble methods and hyperparameter settings on the performance.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect that our adaptive learning rate scheduling method will improve the forecasting performance by allowing the model to adapt to changing loss landscapes and data distributions, but we are also aware of the potential risk of oscillations or decreased stability in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Study of Different Memory Replay Techniques for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comparative study to evaluate the performance of various memory replay methods, including window-based, batch-based, and urgency-based replay, on online time series forecasting tasks using real-world datasets, and investigate the impact of different replay parameters, such as buffer size and replay rate, on the forecasting performance.
CONTROLS: We will use different replay methods as the adaptation mechanism in our online time series forecasting framework and compare their performance against a baseline that does not use any memory replay.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: We expect that using memory replay techniques will improve the forecasting performance by capturing and adapting to non-stationarities in the data, but we are also aware that it may also introduce additional noise or complexities in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Delayed Feedback Impact on Online Time Series Forecasting and Gradient-based Updates
PROPOSAL: We will simulate delayed feedback in our online time series forecasting framework and investigate the impact of delayed feedback on the forecasting performance, as well as the accuracy and stability of gradient-based updates, using real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our online time series forecasting framework with delayed feedback to a baseline that receives immediate feedback and investigate the effect of different feedback delays on the forecasting performance.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect that delayed feedback will negatively impact forecasting performance, especially for longer forecast horizons, and may also lead to instability in gradient-based updates, but we are also interested in investigating potential strategies to mitigate these effects.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Revision of the Development of a New Online Gradient Descent Method with Ensemble-based Adaptive Learning Rate Scheduling
PROPOSAL: We will extend the development of our online gradient descent method to incorporate additional techniques for addressing delayed feedback, such as gradient normalization, delayed gradient accumulation, and prediction horizon-based update schedules, and evaluate their impact on forecasting performance using real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our extended online gradient descent method against the original baseline and other online gradient descent variants that address delayed feedback.
COST: 6600
PREDICTION: We expect that incorporating techniques addressing delayed feedback will improve forecasting performance and stability, but may also introduce additional computational overhead or memory requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Online Time Series Forecasting using Low-Rank Weight Transfer
PROPOSAL: We will develop a robust online time series forecasting framework that employs low-rank weight transfer to capture underlying patterns in the data, and evaluate its performance on real-world datasets with varying levels of concept drift and noise.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our low-rank weight transfer method against state-of-the-art online time series forecasting techniques and investigate the impact of different low-rank constraints and regularization techniques on forecasting performance.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: We expect that low-rank weight transfer will improve forecasting performance by capturing underlying patterns in the data, but may also introduce additional computational overhead or risk of overfitting in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will provide a theoretical analysis of the dynamic regret for online time series forecasting algorithms, and derive regret bounds for specific algorithms, such as online gradient descent and low-rank weight transfer, under different types of data drift and noise.
CONTROLS: We will consider a variety of data drift scenarios and compare the regret bounds of different algorithms to understand their relative performance and identify suitable algorithms for specific use cases.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: We expect that our theoretical analysis will provide insights into the trade-offs between forecasting performance and algorithm stability, but may also reveal limitations of existing algorithms under certain data drift scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of Online Time Series Forecasting Algorithms on Real-World Multi-Step Forecasting Tasks
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experimental evaluation of the online time series forecasting algorithms proposed in this study, including model component adaptation, distribution shift normalization, low-rank weight transfer, and others, on real-world multi-step forecasting tasks across different domains, such as traffic flow, electricity consumption, and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of these algorithms against state-of-the-art online and offline time series forecasting methods and investigate their robustness to different types of data drift and noise.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: We expect that our experimental evaluation will provide comprehensive insights into the performance and robustness of online time series forecasting algorithms in real-world settings, but may also reveal challenges and limitations of these algorithms in certain scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-Source Implementation and Code Reusability Analysis of Online Time Series Forecasting Framework
PROPOSAL: We will create an open-source implementation of the online time series forecasting framework developed in this study, and perform a code reusability analysis to evaluate the ease of adoption and extension of the framework by the research and industry communities.
CONTROLS: We will compare the code reusability of our framework against existing open-source online time series forecasting frameworks and investigate the potential for code reuse and adaptation across different domains.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect that our open-source implementation will contribute to the advancement of the online time series forecasting field by making our framework and findings accessible to a broader audience, but may also require additional effort to document and maintain the codebase.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Exploring Hybrid Retrieval with a Lightweight Dense Text Retriever
PROPOSAL: Implement the ColPali-based late-interaction multimodal retriever as the primary retriever, paired with a lightweight dense text retriever (RoBERTa-base encoders with bio-embeddings) fine-tuned on a text-based document retrieval dataset (MS MARCO, 30,000 documents).
CONTROLS: Baseline ColPali-based retriever alone, ablation of the lightweight text retriever and comparison with pre-trained text encoders (e.g T5).
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The combined retriever should improve retrieval quality over the baseline ColPali-based retriever, while maintaining acceptable online latency and reducing storage requirements; potential failure point: the lightweight text retriever may struggle with purely visional queries or longer documents.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Hybrid Retrieval with Non-Parametric Aggregation
PROPOSAL: At query time, aggregate the similarity scores from the ColPali-based retriever and the lightweight dense text retriever using a non-parametric kernel-based aggregation method, such as a Gaussian kernel or a weighted average of similarities, learned from a set of diverse anchor points (high-quality matches and mismatches) pre-computed across both models.
CONTROLS: Comparison with standard weighted sum and/or Hadamard fusion; ablation study to remove the kernel-based aggregation.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: This method should effectively combine the signals of both retrievers, improving retrieval quality while preserving low latency, but may suffer from overfitting or difficulties in robustly calculating the similarity kernels; a clearer understanding of its strengths and limitations will provide insights for subsequent proposals.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Evaluation Protocol for Comparison of Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Establish an evaluation protocol to compare the performance of the proposed hybrid retrievers with their baseline and ablation counterparts, including the use of well-established metrics in the context of visual document retrieval, such as recall, precision, and Mean Average Precision (MAP), at different retrieval thresholds. Additionally, a series of user studies should be conducted to assess the relevance and helpfulness of retrieved documents in practical scenarios.
CONTROLS: Evaluation on different datasets (e.g., MS MARCO, PubMed, arXiv), comparison with state-of-the-art baselines, and ablation studies to validate the contribution of each component.
COST: 16200
PREDICTION: The evaluation protocol will provide a thorough assessment of the proposed hybrid retrievers, including their strengths and limitations, and will serve as a foundation for future improvements and extensions; potential failure point: the evaluation protocol might not accurately capture the practical relevance of retrieved documents.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Learning to Combine Heterogeneous Representations with Deep Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: Develop a deep neural network-based approach to dynamically combine the representations from the ColPali-based retriever and the lightweight dense text retriever, learn to weigh and fuse them in a way that adapts to the specific query and document pairs, and jointly optimize the objectives of both models during training.
CONTROLS: Comparison with traditional hybrid aggregation methods, study of the impact of different architectures and loss functions on the performance of the combined model, and ablation study to evaluate the relative importance of each component.
COST: 24300
PREDICTION: This approach should enable the system to learn an optimal way of combining the strengths of both retrievers, but may require extensive training time and may not generalize well to unseen data; potential failure point: the model might suffer from overfitting or may not find a good balance between the two representations.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Anchor Points in Hybrid Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Identify and investigate the role of anchor points in the hybrid retrieval framework, specifically the importance of using high-quality matches and mismatches as anchor points in the non-parametric aggregation method, and their impact on the performance of the system. This includes studying the properties and characteristics of effective anchor points, and designing new algorithms to efficiently select and use anchor points.
CONTROLS: Comparative study of different anchor points selection methods, evaluation of the robustness of the system to varying anchor points quality, and ablation study to quantify the contribution of anchor points to the overall performance.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: This investigation will help to better understand the strengths and weaknesses of the hybrid retrieval framework, and potentially lead to improvements in its performance and robustness; potential failure point: the importance of anchor points may be overestimated, and other factors might have a significant impact on the results.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Axiomatic Framework for Hybrid Retrieval Aggregation Methods
PROPOSAL: Develop an axiomatic framework that provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the properties and behaviors of different hybrid retrieval aggregation methods, focusing on conditions such as non-negativity, monotonicity, and subadditivity, and derive bounds and guarantees for the performance of these methods, offering a systematic way to design and evaluate new aggregation techniques.
CONTROLS: Comparative study of different axiomatic frameworks, evaluation of the impact of axiomatic properties on the aggregation methods' performance, and ablation study to quantify the contribution of each axiom.
COST: 48600
PREDICTION: This framework will provide a rigorous and principled approach to the design and evaluation of hybrid retrieval methods, but may require advanced mathematical and computational tools for its implementation, and might lead to overly conservative or restrictive aggregation methods.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Experimental Analysis of Practical Deployment Strategies for Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Conduct an experimental analysis of different strategies for deploying hybrid retrievers in real-world settings, including cloud, on-premise, and edge deployments, and evaluate the impact of factors such as query volume, document size, and index updates on the performance and scalability of these systems, aiming to identify best practices for practical deployments.
CONTROLS: Comparative study of different deployment architectures, evaluation of the impact of various operational factors on system performance, and ablation study to quantify the contribution of each factor.
COST: 72900
PREDICTION: This analysis will provide valuable insights into the practical deployment of hybrid retrievers, but may require collaboration with domain experts and access to real-world operational data, and might lead to conflicting results due to differences in deployment scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: Compositionality in Hybrid Retrieval: A Model-Agnostic Approach
PROPOSAL: Develop a model-agnostic approach to compose and combine multiple hybrid retrievers, designed to preserve the strengths of each individual model while accounting for their interactions and dependencies, and test its effectiveness on a range of real-world and synthetic datasets, aiming to provide a flexible and scalable framework for dynamic hybrid retrieval systems.
CONTROLS: Comparative study of different composition mechanisms, evaluation of the impact of aggregation methods and anchor points on composed models, and ablation study to quantify the contribution of each approach.
COST: 138600
PREDICTION: This work will provide a powerful and flexible framework for composing hybrid retrievers, but may require advanced model-agnostic techniques and possibly some interdisciplinary collaboration, and might lead to overly complex or stochastic models that are difficult to interpret or analyze.
